speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: By developing more attractive career pathways and strengthening the professional recognition and accreditation of engineering skills and expertise, we aim to attract more locals to join the engineering profession.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Engineering will remain a meaningful and respectable profession as we strive for economic and social progress in our next phase of development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The tripartite partners will reach out to more Singaporeans to take up engineering as their career of choice.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Since engineers are so important, I would like to ask how many engineers and engineering positions in Government agencies and Statutory Boards, are filled by foreigners?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Is there a plan to just employ Singaporeans in Government agencies and Statutory Boards?

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Employment of engineers will be based on skill sets.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Some skill sets are, for example, software skill sets.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We will also do our best to make sure that our local engineers are given a fair chance and opportunity to take up positions.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Their skills are applicable broadly across different sectors.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Most of the engineers, if they go to the technical field, they can find job opportunities.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Many of these jobs are covered by engineers, even including the non-functional skills too.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We respect the engineering profession, and we feel that engineering skills and engineers themselves need to be recognised and rewarded.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: It has to be based on two fronts: to make sure that engineers continue to stay in their sector and to have the technical skills.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: From the enterprise perspective, they need to have good human resources (HR) practices.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: These HR practices could mean identifying these engineers as human capital to be invested in and also to make sure that they can continue to deliver value.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: They need to have career paths, wage ladders, and good salary and progression plans for them.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Industry as a whole will depend on the Sectoral Manpower Plan and the tripartite committee to look at the skills sets and the skills of the future to cover the skills gaps, so that we can build up the pipeline between schools and institutions with the industry.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We need to build up more engineers for the sectors.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: That is exactly how we have been approaching it.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I think the Minister of State did not answer my first question.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: How many engineering positions in Government agencies and Statutory Boards are filled by foreigners?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I just want to ask if the Ministry has any plans to bring back engineers who have left the profession.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: And what are the incentives and programmes that will attract these engineers back into the profession again?

speaker: Mdm Speaker
